title: Quantization variant scaling: batch-size & long-context tail latency analysis (FP8/INT8 calibration + accuracy validation)
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Goal: Produce a reproducible benchmarking bundle that quantifies how FP8 and INT8 quantized variants interact with batching and long-context workloads, focusing on tail latency (p95/p99), throughput, and end-to-end quality degradation after calibration. Deliverables: benchmark matrix, calibration artifact bundle, accuracy validation report vs float baseline, and a short runbook for interpreting results and recommended quant profiles for production rollout.
test_matrix: Quant variants: FP8-per-channel, FP8-per-tensor, INT8-symmetric, INT8-affine
Calibration modes: per-layer static (KL), per-channel static (min-max+clipping), dynamic per-batch activation calibration
KV cache scenarios: cold-start (no cache) and warm-start (full KV cache)
Hardware: A100-80GB (single GPU), H100-80GB (single GPU), 2xA100 multi-GPU (baseline distributed), CPU-only baseline for perf delta
Workloads: single-stream chat (low concurrency), multi-stream batched inference (high throughput), summarization evaluation (long input), embedding/rerank microbench
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark runs reproducible with CI job that checks p95/p99 for defined matrix
Accuracy delta for recommended quant profile <= 1.5% relative degradation on primary eval set
Tail latency regression vs float baseline <= 20% for batch sizes 1-8; document trade-offs for larger batch sizes
Provide clear recommendation table mapping workload pattern -> quant profile (FP8/INT8) with notes on calibration mode
Artifacts (calibration tables, scripts, perf logs) uploaded to GH release and referenced in runbook
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: aligned with Research (Aditi Shah) and Console (Riley) on primary eval sets and visibility requirements.
2026-03-04 - Decision: run FP8-per-channel and INT8-affine as primary comparators; FP8-per-tensor as an exploratory control. Reason: per-channel FP8 showed lower accuracy variance in early probes.
2026-03-06 - Early perf results (A100): FP8 variants reduce tokens/sec variance but show a 12% p99 tail increase at batch=1 for long-context 8k seq. Need to isolate KV cache effects.
2026-03-08 - Mitigation: added warm-start runs to separate cold cache penalties. Also added dynamic activation calibration experiment to see runtime correction impact.
2026-03-10 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/412 - benchmark harness additions and new perf parsers. Assigned to Riley for review.
2026-03-11 - Review notes from Infra: add H100 run and include token emission distribution histograms to catch pathological slowdowns. Also requested cost estimates for each profile.
Next steps: complete H100 runs (Miguel), consolidate accuracy diffs into a single table for PM review, and draft recommendation matrix for runtime-1.20 release notes.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Calibration fails to generalize across workloads -> Mitigation: keep per-workload calibration artifacts and record applicability notes
Risk: Tail latency regressions at batch=1 for FP8 -> Mitigation: prioritize kernel-level micro-optimizations and consider automatic fallback policy in Smart Routing
Risk: Cost estimates understate real infra expense for H100 -> Mitigation: capture real cloud consumption and include 95th percentile cost projection
